name: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling. An HPA scales a Deployment's replicas between min and max to hold a target metric (e.g. CPU %). It reads pod metrics and compares usage to the pod's resource REQUEST — so the target workload must declare a CPU request or the HPA reports <unknown>. Create an HPA, then fix one stuck at <unknown>. Graded on the HPA object and the target's request (this bench has no metrics-server, so live scaling isn't graded — the exam checks the object).

questions.title: Autoscale a Deployment on CPU
questions.teach:
An **HPA** targets a workload (`scaleTargetRef`) and keeps a metric near a target by adjusting replicas within `[minReplicas, maxReplicas]`. For CPU utilization it computes `usage / request` per pod — so the **target Deployment must set a CPU request**. The fast path is `kubectl autoscale deploy <name> --cpu-percent=<n> --min=<a> --max=<b>`.

**Gotcha:** CPU `averageUtilization` is a **percent of the request**, not millicores. No request on the pods ⇒ the HPA can't compute ⇒ targets show `<unknown>` and it won't scale.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `hpa-learn`, Deployment `web` (nginx, CPU request `100m`) already exists. Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler `web` targeting it: min `2`, max `5`, CPU average utilization `70%`.

Target: HPA `web` scales Deployment `web` with minReplicas 2, maxReplicas 5, CPU target 70%.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n hpa-learn autoscale deployment web --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=5`. Check: `kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n hpa-learn autoscale deployment web --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=5
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web

verification.description: HPA web -> Deployment web, min 2, max 5, CPU 70%

questions.eli5:
Picture a coffee shop that can call in extra baristas when it gets busy and send them home when it's quiet. A **HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA)** is the manager who does that for your app: it watches how hard each "barista" (pod) is working and adds or removes baristas to keep everyone at a comfortable busy-ness.

You give the manager three rules:
- **min** = never fewer than this many baristas (here **2**),
- **max** = never more than this many (here **5**),
- a **target** = keep each barista around **70% busy**.

If baristas are at 90%, the manager hires more (up to 5). If they're at 30%, it sends some home (down to 2). The one-liner that sets this up is `kubectl autoscale deployment web --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=5`.

Here's the subtle part: "70% busy" is **70% of what?** The HPA measures each pod's CPU use as a **percentage of the CPU the pod *asked for*** (its **request**). So the pod's request is the "full shift" the percentage is measured against. That's why the target Deployment `web` already declares a CPU request of `100m` — without a request, the manager has no idea what "busy" even means.

**Watch out for:**

- **The percentage is of the pod's CPU *request*, not of a whole CPU core.** `70%` of a `100m` request means target ~`70m` per pod.
- **No CPU request on the pods ⇒ the HPA can't compute ⇒ it shows `<unknown>`** and won't scale. (That's the next lesson's bug.)
- **min and max are hard limits** — the HPA never scales below min or above max.
- The HPA points at the **Deployment** (`scaleTargetRef`), and it edits that Deployment's replica count — don't set `replicas` by hand once an HPA owns it.
- Real scaling also needs a **metrics-server** running; without it the HPA has no data to read.
questions.deepDive:
## HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU — full rundown

### The one-sentence model
An **HPA** watches a workload's pod metrics and adjusts `replicas` within `[minReplicas, maxReplicas]` to keep an observed metric near a target. For CPU utilization it computes **`usage ÷ request`** per pod — so the **target pods must declare a CPU request**, or the HPA reports `<unknown>`.

### The scaling formula
```
desiredReplicas = ceil( currentReplicas × ( currentMetricValue / desiredMetricValue ) )
```
For `averageUtilization`, `currentMetricValue` is the mean across pods of `(cpu usage / cpu request) × 100`. Example: 4 pods averaging 140% against a 70% target → `ceil(4 × 140/70)` = `8`, capped at `maxReplicas`.

### The fast path
```bash
kubectl -n hpa-learn autoscale deployment web --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=5
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web          # TARGETS shows <current>%/70%
```

### Equivalent manifest (autoscaling/v2)
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: hpa-learn
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: web
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 5
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
```

### `kubectl autoscale` flags
| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--cpu-percent=70` | Target CPU `averageUtilization` (% of **request**) |
| `--min=2` | `minReplicas` floor |
| `--max=5` | `maxReplicas` ceiling (required) |
| `--name` | HPA name (defaults to target name) |

> `--cpu-percent` creates the old-style CPU metric; the server stores it as an `autoscaling/v2` Resource/Utilization metric.

### CPU target types: Utilization vs AverageValue
| `target.type` | Meaning | Needs request? |
|---|---|---|
| `Utilization` | Percent of the pod's CPU **request** | **Yes** |
| `AverageValue` | Absolute millicores per pod (e.g. `200m`) | No |

`--cpu-percent` always produces `Utilization`, which is why a request is mandatory here.

### What `<unknown>` means
`kubectl get hpa` TARGETS column shows `<unknown>/70%` when the HPA cannot compute the current value. Two causes:
1. **Target pods have no CPU request** (can't compute utilization) — the exam cause.
2. **No metrics-server** / metrics API not serving data.

### Inspect / debug
```bash
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web
kubectl -n hpa-learn describe hpa web          # Events + "unable to get metrics" reasons
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web -o yaml
kubectl top pods -n hpa-learn                  # needs metrics-server
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Utilization % is of the request, not a full core.** 70% of a `100m` request ≈ `70m`.
- **No request → `<unknown>`**, and the HPA won't scale. Fix is on the Deployment's container, not the HPA.
- **Don't hand-set `replicas`** on a Deployment owned by an HPA — the controller fights you. Omit `replicas` or let the HPA own it.
- **`--max` is required**; `--min` defaults to 1 if omitted.
- **Scale-down is deliberately slow** (default `stabilizationWindowSeconds` 300s) to avoid flapping; scale-up is faster.
- On this bench there is **no metrics-server**, so live scaling isn't graded — the exam checks the HPA **object** (target ref, min/max, 70%).
- Use **`autoscaling/v2`** for manifests; `v2beta*` is removed and `v1` only supports CPU.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n hpa-learn autoscale deployment web --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=5
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web
# verify object
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa web \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.minReplicas}/{.spec.maxReplicas} cpu={.spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization}'; echo
```

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: HPA stuck at <unknown>
questions.teach:
An HPA whose CPU target reads `<unknown>` almost always means the **target pods have no CPU request** (so utilization can't be computed). The fix is on the **Deployment**: add a CPU request to its container; the HPA then reads metrics and can scale.

**Gotcha:** fix the Deployment's pod template (`resources.requests.cpu`), not the HPA. (A truly missing metrics-server also causes `<unknown>`, but on the exam the cause is the missing request.)
questions.prompt:
Setup created Deployment `api` (no CPU request) and HPA `api` targeting it — so the HPA can't compute utilization (`<unknown>`). Fix it so the HPA can work: give `api`'s container a CPU request of `100m`.

Target: Deployment `api`'s container has `resources.requests.cpu` set (e.g. `100m`), and HPA `api` still targets it.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deploy api --requests=cpu=100m` (or edit the Deployment). The HPA `api` already exists; you're fixing the target's missing request.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deployment api --requests=cpu=100m
kubectl -n hpa-learn rollout status deploy/api
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa api

verification.description: Deployment api now has a CPU request; HPA api targets it

questions.eli5:
Back to the coffee-shop manager (the HPA) who scales baristas up and down to keep everyone around "70% busy." But there's a problem: the manager's dashboard says **`<unknown>`** instead of a busy-ness number. It has no idea how hard anyone is working, so it just freezes and never adds or removes baristas.

Why? Remember, "busy-ness" is measured as a **percentage of what each pod asked for** (its CPU **request**). The Deployment `api` was created **without a CPU request** — so there's no "full shift" to measure against. 70% of *nothing* is undefined, so the dashboard reads `<unknown>`.

The fix is **not** on the manager (the HPA) — it's on the workers. You go edit the **Deployment `api`** and give its container a CPU request, e.g. `100m`. Once each pod declares "I asked for 100m," the manager can finally compute "this pod is using 70m, that's 70% busy," and it starts working again.

The quick command: `kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deploy api --requests=cpu=100m`.

**Watch out for:**

- **`<unknown>` almost always = the target pods have no CPU request.** Fix the Deployment's `resources.requests.cpu`, not the HPA.
- **Don't edit the HPA** trying to fix this — the HPA is fine; the missing request is on the Deployment.
- Changing the Deployment's resources **rolls the pods** (new pods with the request); wait for the rollout to finish.
- **A missing metrics-server** also shows `<unknown>` — but on the exam (and this lab) the cause is the missing request.
- The request is what the percentage is measured against, so pick a sensible value (`100m` here).
questions.deepDive:
## Fixing an HPA stuck at `<unknown>` — full rundown

### The one-sentence model
A CPU-utilization HPA computes **`usage ÷ request`** per pod. If the target pods have **no CPU request**, there's no denominator — the HPA can't compute utilization and reports **`<unknown>`**. The fix lives on the **Deployment** (add `resources.requests.cpu`), not on the HPA.

### Diagnosis
```bash
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa api
# NAME   REFERENCE        TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
# api    Deployment/api   <unknown>/70%   1         5         1

kubectl -n hpa-learn describe hpa api
# Conditions: ScalingActive  False  FailedGetResourceMetric
# "missing request for cpu" (or "unable to get metrics for resource cpu")
```
`describe` names the reason. Two distinct causes produce `<unknown>`:

| Cause | describe hint | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Target container has no CPU request** | `missing request for cpu` | Add `resources.requests.cpu` to the Deployment |
| **metrics-server absent / not ready** | `unable to get metrics` / `no metrics returned` | Install/repair metrics-server |

On the CKA exam and this bench the cause is the **missing request**.

### Why the request is mandatory
`type: Utilization` means "percent of the pod's request." With no request the ratio `usage/request` is division by an undefined value, so the metric is unavailable. (Contrast `type: AverageValue`, which uses absolute millicores and needs no request — but `--cpu-percent` always creates `Utilization`.)

### The fix — on the Deployment
```bash
# fastest
kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deployment api --requests=cpu=100m
kubectl -n hpa-learn rollout status deploy/api
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa api        # TARGETS should leave <unknown> once metrics flow
```
Equivalent manifest patch on the container:
```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: <container>
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
```
Or `kubectl -n hpa-learn edit deployment api` and add the `resources.requests.cpu` block.

### `kubectl set resources` flags
| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--requests=cpu=100m` | Set the CPU request (what the HPA divides by) |
| `--requests=cpu=100m,memory=64Mi` | Set multiple requests at once |
| `--limits=cpu=250m` | Set limits (not needed for the HPA fix) |
| `-c <name>` | Target a specific container |

### Verify the fix
```bash
kubectl -n hpa-learn get deploy api \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.cpu}'; echo   # 100m
kubectl -n hpa-learn get hpa api                 # HPA still references Deployment/api
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Fix the Deployment, not the HPA.** The HPA object is correct; the missing request is on the target's pod template.
- **`<unknown>` has two causes** — confirm with `describe hpa` before assuming. This lab = missing request.
- **Setting resources rolls the Deployment** — new pods are created with the request; wait for `rollout status`.
- **Don't set the request on the HPA** — HPAs have no resources field.
- Even with the request added, TARGETS may stay `<unknown>` here because **this bench has no metrics-server** — grading checks that the request exists and the HPA still targets `api`.
- Keep the value **reasonable** (`100m`); the utilization percentage is relative to it.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n hpa-learn describe hpa api            # confirm "missing request for cpu"
kubectl -n hpa-learn set resources deploy api --requests=cpu=100m
kubectl -n hpa-learn rollout status deploy/api
```
